correctness.rationale: Direct orthogonal decomposition yields error squared ||r||²+||(lambda p-sqrt(W)Z r)/(W+lambda)||², with W chi-square and Z Gaussian independent. The Gaussian-angle integral gives mean ||r||²=ab, mean ||p||²=a²-ab+b². Differentiated risk has strictly positive W-factor and one unique zero at lambda=ab/(a²-ab+b²). Chi-square negative moments yield exact p<s cutoff and E1/W=1/(s-2); positive ridge bounds all moments. Isotropic trace and beta tail follow by orthogonality. Embedded verifier uses symbolic identities and 6049 deterministic direct/analytic comparisons; those corroborate but are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A natural low-rank stage approximation with independent left and right Gaussian sketches needs sensible small-sample regularization: for one/two left test rows zero ridge has infinite mean-square error, while the theorem supplies finite risk and an exactly optimal, sketch-count-independent positive penalty for all s>=1. It also identifies a quantitative clash between Frobenius approximation quality and trace fidelity on isotropic matrices, clarifying what regularization can and cannot preserve. The exact 2x2 benchmark is limited but motivated by recurrent generalized Nyström stage approximation, rather than an arbitrary slice.
